utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Case Number IT-01-47-T, the Prosecutor versus Enver Hadzihasanovic and Amir Kubura.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we have the appearances for the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours, Counsel, and everyone in and around the courtroom. For the Prosecution, Tecla Henry-Benjamin and Daryl Mundis, assisted by Andres Vatter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have the appearances for Defence counsel in the usual order.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours. On behalf of General Hadzihasanovic, Edina Residovic, lead counsel, and Stephane Bourgon, co-counsel. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the other Defence team.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. On behalf of Mr. Kubura, Rodney Dixon, Fahrudin Ibrisimovic, and Nermin Mulalic, our legal assistant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to greet everyone present, members of the Prosecution, Defence counsel, the accused, and everyone else in the courtroom. I believe that there is an issue concerning tendering a document into evidence. I will give the floor to General Hadzihasanovic's Defence counsel in that case. Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. President. Good morning, Madam Judge. Good morning, Your Honour. Unfortunately I don't have the document on me. The issue concerned the documents that we wanted to tender. I don't have them with me. I forgot them in my office this morning. I apologise, Mr. President. We'll deal with this issue at the next hearing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Have you spoken to the Prosecution to obtain their agreement in --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There are no problems, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. In that case we'll call the witness into the courtroom. Mr. Usher, could you bring the witness into the courtroom, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, sir. I would first like to make sure that you are receiving the interpretation of what I am saying into your own language. If so, please tell us that you can understand us.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness's answer wasn't audible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, you've been called here as a witness for Mr. Kubura's Defence. Before you take the solemn declaration, could you tell me your date of birth, your place of birth, your first and last name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My name is Suad Jusovic. I was born on the 3rd of November, 1965, in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What are you by profession?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am currently waiting for my pension that should regulate my status in the army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In 1992 and 1993 did you have a profession of any kind or military position, if you are a member of the military? What position did you hold in the military and which unit were you in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was the commander of a platoon and of a company in the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Have you already testified before an international or national court about the events that took place in your country in 1992 and 1993, or is this the first time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have never testified before, but I have given a statement about war crimes in Prijedor. I gave the statement to the authorities in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please read out the solemn declaration that the usher will show to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You may sit down. Before I give the floor to the Defence, who will commence their examination-in-chief, I would like to provide you with some information. You will first have to answer questions that will be put to you by Mr. Kubura's Defence. We have been informed that they will need about an hour and a half for their examination-in-chief. It might take a little longer or a little shorter, but that's a rough estimate. After this stage has been completed, the Prosecution, who are to your right, and they will conduct what we call their cross-examination. It's a well-known Anglo-Saxon procedure and it is within this framework that you will have to answer questions that will last as long as the examination-in-chief. Then, Brigadier Kubura's [as interpreted] Defence or the other Defence team may ask you additional questions and the three Judges sitting before you may also ask you questions at any time. But as a rule, we prefer to wait for both parties to complete their examination and cross-examination and then we will put questions to you to clarify some of your answers. We might also put questions to you because we believe there are certain gaps that need to be filled, certain gaps in your testimony. I would also like to draw your attention to other important points. As you have given the solemn declaration, you should not give false testimony. There is another very complicated provision I should inform you of. You may also refuse to answer a question if you believe the answer could be used against you at a subsequent date. But in such a case - and we have never had such cases to date - in such a case the Chamber may compel you to answer the question, but you are granted immunity. This is a provision contained in the Rules, the purpose of which is to enable witnesses to contribute to establishing the truth. If you find that a question is too complicated, don't hesitate to ask the party putting the question to you to rephrase it. The procedure followed here is basically an oral procedure and there is a screen where everything that is said is transcribed. You might also be shown documents, military documents, either to identify them or to comment on them, to comment on military documents as a member of the military. Roughly speaking, this is how we will be proceeding today. If there are any problems, do inform us of the fact. And we will be having two breaks in the course of the hearing. This should allow you to -- there seems to be a problem with the earphones. Everything is fine?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Everything is fine now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I was saying, we will be having two 20- to 25-minute breaks and we will be finishing the hearing at 1.45. This means that it won't be necessary for you to staying in The Hague to appear for the hearing on Monday, providing that the parties adhere to the schedule. Without wasting anymore time, I will now give the floor to Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Jusovic, in response to a question put to you by the Presiding Judge you said that in 1992 and 1993 you were in the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Where were you when the war broke out?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: I was in Oftina Prijedor, western Bosnian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: On the 1st of April 1992 -- In April 1992?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: What happened then with you then?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: I had then come from Switzerland for a holiday. I could not return. The Serbian and Montenegrin aggressor had penetrated into Oftina Prijedor and Oftina Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Were you arrested during those events?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, on the 28th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: What happened after that?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: I was then taken to the Omarska camp from the 28th of May up until the 17th of August. I think I was in Omarska. And from the 17th to the 21st of August I was in Trnopolje camp.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: When did you come to Travnik and how?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: On the 21st of August, 1992, I arrived there in a convoy. And between 22 -- 220 and 250 people were taken from the convoy at Koricanska Stijena and were killed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you joined the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade, did you have an establishment post?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: When I entered the 7th Muslim Brigade I didn't have an establishment post; I was an ordinary soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: After that, in 1992 and 1993 -- let me just interrupt you. Could we just pause between my questions and your answers for the sake of the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Around the beginning of December I became the commander of a platoon. And in mid-December 1992 I became the commander of the 2nd Company.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Of which company?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Of the 2nd Company of the 1st Mountain Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: The 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade. Did it have its zone of responsibility in the area of Travnik?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. On Bijelo Bucje. To the right there was Kazici and to the left there was elevation 1268.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we would like to use a number of documents with this witness, including a map. With your leave, could these documents be shown to the witness as well as the map. The map is on the ELMO -- could you place the map on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: First, Mr. Jusovic, I would like to ask you the following. The 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade was part of the Bosnian Krajina OG. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Please have a look at the map. A while ago you said that the zone of responsibility of the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade was the Kazici elevation, or rather Bijelo Bucje. Could you point to these locations.

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: We can see the village of Bijelo Bucje here. To the right there is the village of Kazici. Here you have a slope and you arrive to elevation 268 here; there was the zone of responsibility of the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Could you take a felt tip and encircle the area you have referred to.

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Could you mark it with the letter A or number 1.

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jusovic, how many soldiers were there in your battalion at that time? How many soldiers did your company have?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Our battalion had up to 50 and 65 per cent of its strength right up until the end of its time within the 7th Muslim Brigade. In my company there was 60 to 70 soldiers on a permanent basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us how duties were performed in the zone of responsibility. How did the men rotate and how frequently?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: The 1st Battalion had four companies, and in those companies they had logistics support. And every 15 days, two companies were on the lines and two companies or on leave. And then the companies that were on leave would leave their equipment and weapons in the barracks and go home. Transport was organised in buses, and some of them drove home or walked home.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Where were your -- where were the battalion and your companies in the summer?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: The 1st Battalion was in the zone of responsibility of the battalion and in the Travnik barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Where was your company at that time?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: My company was then in the Bijelo Bucje zone of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Until when was your company in Bijelo Bucje?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: It was there until the 23rd of May, 1993, from the 12th of February until April [as interpreted] because we weren't able to rotate men because of certain problems we had within the unit. Some went on leave to Zenica, Nemila, Vitez, Bugojno and were not able to return from there. There were problems with the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, there's an error in the transcript. Page 9, line 9 it says from February until April and the witness said from February until the 23rd of May, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jusovic, have you heard of the village of Miletici?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: I've heard of the village of Miletici as three months -- I heard about it three months after the crime in Miletici. It was only when I arrived there later. I heard about it three months later.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: On the 24th of April, 1993, in the afternoon did you arrive in the village of Miletici and do you know whether anyone from the battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade was in Miletici at that time on that day?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: No, I couldn't be in Miletici because I had a zone of responsibility where I was holding the defence line. And as far as I know, I was familiar with the events. No one from the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade participated in those activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know where the 4th Company was at the time, at that time?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: It was in the village of Poculica, near Sivrino Selo, Sivrino village, because they were all from that area and they had been subordinated to the 325th Mountain Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Did the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade have an organised unit in the Bila Valley?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: It didn't have an organised unit in the Bila Valley because we had ten members from there -- we had ten members from there who were part of the 1st Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Where were your battalion located?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: It was located in the Travnik barracks. It was billeted in the Travnik barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: And the battalion command?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: It was deployed above the old department store of Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: You said on the 23rd of May, 1993, you returned from a shift in your zone of responsibility in Bijelo Bucje. Where did you go then?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: We then received an order from the command of Bosnian Krajina OG, from Commander Alagic. We were ordered to go on leave and the 3rd Battalion of the 17th Vitez and Krajina Brigade replaced us afterwards. We arrived in the barracks. We left our equipment and weapons there and the soldiers left on leave and went to Travnik. They went to their homes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Were there any men from the 7th Muslim Brigade and the 1st Battalion who had remained in Bijelo Bucje?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, a platoon, a logistics platoon remained there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: After the order that you received from General Alagic for your unit to go on leave, what happened?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: About the 27th or 28th of May we received an order from the commander of the OG, from Commander Alagic, to assemble and to be in the reserve force of the Bosnian Krajina OG.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Where were you deployed?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: In the barracks. At the time there were members from the 1st Motorised Company who lived in Travnik, but they didn't have their own company because their company was on leave. So some of those men were resubordinated to my company. That was about -- there were about 25 men.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: How many men did you have under your command then?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Around 85.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: When the conflict broke out in Travnik, where were you, Mr. Jusovic?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: We were in the barracks and as ordered by the commander of the Bosnian Krajina OG we were to go to Hajdareve Njive, which is above Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: When were you first engaged in combat activity and when did you go to Hajdareve Njive?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: I think it was on the 5th of June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Where exactly is Hajdareve Njive?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Hajdareve Njive -- I can't see it very well on the screen, so I'm going to look at the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: We'll come to that but I would just like to ask a question. Can you repeat -- can you answer my question, please. In this bundle of documents could you look for the document number 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the sake of the transcript, this is DK number 19 -- I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Could you take a look --

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is not 19 -- rather, it is not 5 but it is 4.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is an extraordinary combat report of the operations group Bosanska Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jusovic, could you look at item 2, the phrase that starts with 1/7.

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Can you read it out.

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: "The 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade is engaged in direction of Hajdareve Njive linking it to itself and covering it with its mortars."

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: What happened afterwards?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: According to the task assigned by the commander, we went to Hajdareve Njive. We took one part of the combat positions, and afterwards we could no longer hold those positions and we withdrew at some point in the morning between 9.00 and 10.00 a.m. and returned to barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Where did you go back to?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: The barracks, because the barracks were not too far away. So it was about 800 metres as the crow flies where the barracks were.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: After that, were you assigned any other tasks by the operatives group -- or rather, let me ask you first: Who was issuing orders to you at that time?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: At that time we received all orders from the operative group Bosanska Krajina, and I myself got my orders from the deputy commander Horo Naim.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: I asked you before what happened after the 5th of June. Were you assigned any other task?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: We were assigned the task to go to the village of Guvna.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Where is this village?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: It is left of Travnik, a kilometre or 200 metres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Were you assigned any tasks on the 8th of June?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: What was this task?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: It was to take Hajdareve Njive again so as to be able to continue in the direction to Gluha Bukovica and Gostilj. Either Gostilj or Gostunj.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Can you take a look at document number 5 now.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the sake of the transcript it is 5465.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: The regular operative report of the command of the Operation Group Bosanska Krajina. On page 2, can you tell us what AGD means.

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: This is the signature of the commander of the Operative Group Bosanska Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Who was the commander?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Mehmed. It was his signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know him personally?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: If you look at the top of the page where it says the command of the Operative Group of Bosanska Krajina, can you see the date? The 8th of June, 1993, at 1900 hours. And could you read out to us the last phrase of this regular operations report, starting with 1/7.

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: "The 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade is active in the area of Hajdareve Njive in the direction of Bukovica."

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Is this regular operations report by General Alagic, does it reflect what you were referring to and does it refer to the combat activities of the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Can you repeat the question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: What you saw in this document, the text that you've just read out, does it reflect what you testified about with regard to the combat activities of the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade on the 8th of June, 1993? Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to ask you to look at the map to your right and show the Trial Chamber and all of us where exactly Hajdareve Njive is located.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just for the sake of the transcript it is 5465, Defence Exhibit P465. I think it has been entered into this transcript in an incorrect way.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, while the witness is looking for what my learned friend asked him to be, I believe there is another mistake on page 10.4. He said that a part was resubordinated of the 325th Brigade and the term "325th Brigade" did not enter the transcript. It is on page 10, line 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that there is some confusion. I don't think that the witness actually mentioned that. I think he said that they were resubordinated to the Operations Group Bosanska Krajina, as far as I understood.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask the colleagues to take a look.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, I do apologise. When we were talking about the -- a company from Poculica. That was it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, I do apologise. That's right. I meant the Battalion.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Hajdareve Njive is right here.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Could you mark it in the same way you did with Bijelo Bucje.

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: How far is Hajdareve Njive from Travnik?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Somewhere between 6 and 800 metres as the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: When you marked Bijelo Bucje you marked it by an A and you have to mark this by a B. After the completion of that combat activities that you've referred to, could you tell us what went on afterwards on that day and the following battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade, that is to say your company in particular?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: My company stayed there throughout the month of August, and in the beginning of September and by the end of September -- or rather, the end -- it is not September, it is the 9th of June -- with the other units we went out of Veljka Bukovica.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters apologise. We took the 9th to mean September but it was the 9th of June, in fact.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We were talking about the units of 4th Battalion of the 17th Krajina Brigade and the TVO [as interpreted] staff Travnik and a part of the 312th Brigade and a part of the police force from Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Where is the place called Sibicara?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: It's at the crossroads over here, in the direction of Travnik and branching off in the other direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Did the 1st Battalion do anything in that area?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They were in that area between the 5th and the 6th of June and the 8th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: How far is Sibicara from Travnik?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: A kilometre.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: You've marked this plant, Sibicara. Could you mark it by a C.

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jusovic, you said that the 4th Company was at Poculica and that you with about 80 soldiers were active in this area of Hajdareve Njive and the area that you've marked here. Where were the other soldiers of the 1st Battalion?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: The 4th Company, I believe, went on the 17th of April or the 17th of May. They went in the direction of the village of Vitez following approval from the deputy commander Horo Naim. As I said, the 1st Company was on leave. They had about 20 soldiers in the village of Nemila. It is in the municipality of Zenica. And they were for the most part members from Jajce who had been displaced and they were refugees and they were in that company. And the part of the company was in Travnik. Between 25 and 30 soldiers were in Travnik and ten soldiers were in a village called Kljaci -- I think it is called Kljaci. And the 3rd Company was in a place called Rostovo and the 1st Company, as I said, was within Travnik itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Could we just clarify this. After what events did Mr. Alagic's [as interpreted] company go to Poculica?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: When those problems happened in Ahmici he left with his company.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Here it says the 17th of April or the 17th of May. Can you specify?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: I think it was the 17th of May. I think that was when he went.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: When did the events at Ahmici take place?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: I have no recollection of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: The events at Ahmici -- no, I withdraw that question. Mr. Jusovic, have you ever heard of a village called Maline?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Did your company or another company from the 1st Battalion ever engage in combat activity in the village Maline?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: It didn't because there were no members from the village of Maline and the other units from the 1st Battalion did not engage in that area of the mountain brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: On the 8th of June, 1993, were you active in that area?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you sign the map that you have marked and indicate the date on which you've done it in a corner.

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On page 17, Mr. President, on line number 6 it should be Adilovic instead of Alagic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you asking for map to be tendered?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we suggest this map to be accepted as a Defence exhibit for Mr. Kubura.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General Hadzihasanovic's Defence team, do you have any comments?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, do your duty.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. So it is Defence document for General Kubura, DK37.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In English, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In English] The exhibit is admitted into evidence under the reference DK37. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jusovic, did you know Ramo Durmis?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: I did know Ramo Durmis from the time when I joined the unit until the 28th or 25th of January, 1993 when we were in the same unit in the same battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Since when had he been in the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: I think until either the 5th or the 10th of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: After what events did he leave?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: After the Visoko operation in the 28th of December, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Was Ramo Durmis the commander of the 1st Company at the time?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: According to what I heard afterwards, he had never been appointed commander of that company. But I don't know how come he held the position of commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Could you take a look at the document in this bundle number 1. It's DK29, for the sake of the transcript. If you take a look at that, names of the commanders of the 1st 2nd, 3rd Company, does it reflect the situation in February 1993?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Is according to this order the commander of the company Mr. Basic, Muhamed?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: And are you indicated as a commander of the company?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could you take a look at the document number 3 here. This is the Prosecution document P77. In item 1 --

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Is it 4?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: No, 1. The following members of the 7th Muslim Brigade have been awarded a monetary incentive. Is your name on this list?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: On the occasion of what event?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: On the occasion of the 28th of December when we participated in the Visegrad action.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: If you take a look at the date, the 14th of April, what happened on that day?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: On this day there were preparations for the day celebrating the army of the BH.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: In number 5 there is your name and you have been awarded this prize?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: On the next page, under number 4, can you take a look at this, B.

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Those are awards to companies which participated in those operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Is it for individuals or units?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: It is for units and the reference is to the 1st Company of the 1st Battalion and its commander, Durmis. And this was the praise given to the 1st Company of the 1st Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jusovic, have you ever been to Mehurici?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: I have never been to Mehurici but I did travel through Mehurici later on because that is where our way to our area of responsibility was to Neokrnje.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Where is Neokrnje?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Neokrnje is away from Mehurici but maybe 30 kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Have you had any contacts with the camp that was located at Mehurici?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: I have never had any contacts with them and I didn't even know where they were exactly, but I did hear that there was somebody in Mehurici.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Once again on page 20, line 4, Mr. President, the witness said it was the anniversary of the setting up of the armed forces with regard to the date in April 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Did you as company commander ever participate or did any of your soldiers ever participate in any activities in which participated any foreign nationals?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: It was not possible in my company because it was mostly a company made of displaced persons and refugees. And we were somewhat different from all the other companies. We were considered as nicer than the others and we had never contacts with them. And they did not offer any help in any operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: And what about the the 1st Battalion?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: There were no foreign nationals in the 1st Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know Mr. Kubura?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: I met Mr. Kubura, I believe, on the 20th or the 25th of January when I came to the barracks at Zenica. And that's how I met him.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know Mr. Koricic?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did see Asim.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: What was his position with the brigade?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: In the beginning he was the brigade commander, I believe, until April. I think he left in April. He left Bosnia in April and I don't think he came back until October of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: What was Mr. Kubura's position?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: According to my information I know he was the Chief of Staff and he carried out those duties and he was appointed as commander of the brigade at some point in the month of August 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Between April and -- I mean the time when Mr. Kubura was appointed commander, did you have any communication with the brigade?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Until the 16th or the 20th June, 1993, so we could not communicate and we did not have any communications.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Can you repeat that once again. Between April and June, as you said, did you have communication with the brigade or not?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: We had communication by phone when phones were working, but we had no other forms of communication.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: When Mr. Koricic came back in October 1993, that's what you said?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Where did he come back to?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: We were in the area of responsibility of Preocica and that's where I met him when he came and was talking to soldiers. So I went and said hello. And on that day or the following day there was a wounding at the village of Sadovace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: And what about --what about your members of the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he came to visit us.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Where exactly was Mr. Koricic wounded?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly. It was in the area above the village of Sadovace.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could you please have a break between the two questions because we can't follow if you speak at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: I think my last question did not enter the transcript so I'm going to repeat it. Was he wounded in the area of responsibility of your company of the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: No, it was in the area of the 325th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: And in that area?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: And in that area there was the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade and that was in the area in which he was wounded.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, microphone, please, for the counsel.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were --

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to ask the Defence with regard to the binder. You have a document number 6 here. You did not show it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not, no. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right then. The other Defence team.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, for the time being we have no questions for this witness. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We still have about 35 minutes left and I'm going to give the floor to the Prosecution for the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, I wonder if I can address the Trial Chamber probably in the absence of the witness at this time, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right then. Usher, can you accompany the witness out of the courtroom and we'll go and get him again in a couple of minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have the floor, Madam.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. President, when the summary was given to me for me to prepare for this witness, I was told that -- or it said, rather, that the witness was the commander of the 1st Company of the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade, and it more or less followed the pattern of the witnesses that went before him. By the time I was ready to prepare for this witness I got an e-mail message saying that there was an error by the Defence and that in fact the witness was commander of the 1st Company of the 2nd Battalion. So I had to switch gears and move to the 2nd Battalion. My cross-examination, therefore, is a little bit different than what would have been done for the 1st Battalion. But since I have been in the courtroom for the first witness and basically had followed the procedures for the second and third witness, I would continue with the cross-examination. But of course it's going to be limited to a certain extent, which I think it's not quite fair to the Prosecution. But I just wanted to alert the Trial Chamber to this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. It is correct that in the summary we indicated that this witness was the commander of the 1st Company. But a few days ago we did inform the Prosecution that this witness was the commander of the 2nd Company and the proof, the exhibit from the Prosecution, indicates that this witness is the commander of the 2nd Company.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Madam Benjamin, apparently the Defence informed you twice that there was a mistake there and that according to the documents coming from the Prosecution itself you should yourselves know that he was the commander of the 2nd Company and not the first one.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: That is true -- the latter part is true because where we were doing the research we were a bit puzzled. But as to the first part -- I mean, I'm here to disagree with my colleague. But the memo, the message, clearly says that he was commander of the 1st Company of the 2nd Battalion. Now, that is completely different for the 1st Company of the 1st Battalion. And so my questions with respect to him were in a different vein. In the light that he was going to speak about Maline and about the foreigners, my questions would have been in a general tune because we couldn't find this witness anywhere in respect on a list with respect to being the commander of the 1st Company of the 1st Battalion. I just wanted to alert the Trial Chamber just in case my cross-examination may appear to be just a little bit outside the scope of the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but DK29 which you have in front of you which was admitted into evidence. Perhaps the registrar could tell us the date when it was admitted into evidence. Mr. Registrar, DK29, when was it admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this document was admitted into evidence on the 12th of April through Witness Terzic. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In DK29 admitted on the 12th of April, reference is made to the fact that the commander of the 2nd Company is the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Except for the fact, Mr. President, that despite my asking for the documents that we were going to be using so that I myself could sort this out, I never received the documents by fax until last night at 9.28. 9.28 I had already left the chambers -- I had already left my office so I got it this morning when I came into court. That is when I got the bulk of documents that the Defence intended to use.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. The documents we've used are not new documents; they've already been admitted. In our summary, apart from the technical error, according to which he was the commander of the 1st Company, in our summary it clearly says that he will be testifying about the fact that the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade was not engaged in Maline, but that it was engaged in Hajdareve Njive and that it was engaged in the village of Miletici. My examination was restricted to this field, and these are only the matters that I addressed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I'll take advantage of the question that you asked to make a following -- the following comment. This does not engage the other Judges. We are dealing with members of the military. I believe that if a case concerns members of the military the Prosecution, which alleges certain violations, should have from the outset presented to the Chamber in the course of the hearings held diagrams of the different bodies, the 7th Brigade, the 17th Krajina Brigade, the 325th, et cetera. If this had been done, you would immediately have been able to indicate in these diagrams the names and the positions of the people concerned and the names of the commanders of companies, because everyone knows a brigade is composed of companies. Companies -- you have brigades, you have battalions, and in battalions you have companies. And it would have been very simple to have for each unit the precise name of the person in charge instead of discovering that on the 14th of April, today, that there's certain ambiguity concerning the name and the person in charge of the 2nd Company of the 1st Battalion of the 7th Brigade. This is something we should have been aware of at the beginning of this case. Having said that, we won't waste any more time. We'll call the witness back into the courtroom for the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I would just like one minute. The Prosecution alleges that Ramo Durmis was the commander of the 1st Company. This is something that we have known from the very beginning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You may sit down. I'll now give the floor to the Prosecution. You may commence with your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Jusovic. My name is Tecla Henry-Benjamin and I am one of the Prosecutors representing the Prosecution in this trial. I'm going to ask you a few questions for the purpose of clarification. If, however, during my interrogation you do not understand what I'm saying or you wish me to repeat the question, please do say and I'll oblige. Thank you. My first question to you would be: Were you ever a member of the Travnik Muslim forces?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: And could you tell me -- or for the benefit of the Trial Chamber could you state exactly when you assumed the role of the first commander of the 1st Battalion -- command of the 1st Company of the 1st Battalion?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Around the 24th of December.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute. Yes, Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, our objection concerns the question. The witness never said that he was the commander of the 1st Company of the 1st Battalion.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was the commander of the 2nd Company on the 24th of December.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: And so I'll ask you this: Just to clarify and for the record, at no time at all were you ever the commander of the 1st Company of the 1st Battalion?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: I was the commander in July or August. I think that that was when I was the commander of the 1st Company.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: July, August of which year?

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: As commander, could you indicate to the Trial Chamber who you recognised as your superior.

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: First there was the battalion commander Hadzic, Fadil. That was between the -- between November 1992 until the 2nd of February, 1993. After that, Ahmed Zubaca was the commander; he held that post for a brief period of time. And then there was Safet Junuzovic. He was the commander from June until November of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: My learned friend asked you about Asim Koricic, do you recall?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: And did there come a time when Asim Koricic was not in command? Did there come a time when he was away from his post?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: I think that that happened towards the end of March and at the beginning of April and continued up until the end of 1993. He then went abroad. He returned in October. I couldn't say whether he was the commander or not at the time because I wasn't in a position to know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: But surely, as commander of your company you must have had certain working relations with somebody who is superior to you. Who would have you been relating to?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the battalion commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: And who was the battalion commander at the time?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: At the time there was a deputy from April to June, but we didn't have a commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: So you're related to your deputy -- you're related to the deputy, to the battalion commander. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Now, you indicated on page 22, line 10 of the transcript that you had no communications between April to June of 1993 with the then-commander. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: And then you further went on to say but you had telephone communications. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The deputy commander of the battalion had such communications. I didn't have any communications.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: During April 1993 and June 1993, did you know Mr. Kubura?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: As I have said, I met Mr. Kubura in January between the 20th and 24th of January when he was the Chief of Staff of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: That's correct, the 24th -- between the 20th and 24th of January you met him. But my question to you: Did you have any communications with Mr. Kubura between the period April 1993 to June 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the answer clearly.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Sir, can you kindly repeat your answer, please, for the benefit of the transcript because the interpreter did not hear your answer.

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: We didn't have any contact. I had no contact with Mr. Amir Kubura during that period of time.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: With respect to the foreigners or the mujahedins, as it's referred to, could you for the benefit of the Trial Chamber explain to us what was your experience with respect to the Mujahedins and the foreigners in Travnik during the period April 1993 to June 1993.

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: They weren't in Travnik during that period of time, so we couldn't have any contact with them nor could we see them in Travnik. As far as I knew they were in Mehurici and some of them were in Bijelo Bucje. They weren't resubordinated to anyone there. They acted independently, so sometimes they would cause problems for the locals up there.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Now, when I said to you could you tell us in Travnik, I meant when you were -- you were based in Travnik, your AOR in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: I'm saying to you that during your time there what was your experience, whether they were in Mehurici or whatever. Could you give us an idea of what transpired.

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Well -- in fact, I knew nothing about them when I arrived from Prijedor. I would only see them walking around time. I would see them in the mosque, but I had no contact with them. So I couldn't say what sort of experience I had of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: I take you mean you didn't have personal contact with the foreigners, Mujahedins. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Okay. A little -- a little further down the road. Are you aware or could you elaborate for the Trial Chamber as to whether soldiers in the 7th Mountain Muslim Brigade received training from foreign fighters or Mujahedins? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, they didn't receive training from those foreigners.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: As far as you know did the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade consist of Muslims?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: The 7th Muslim Brigade was composed exclusively of Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: That's correct. And as far as you know, could you assist us as to the ethnicity of the Muslims in the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Well, they were Bosniaks from Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Would there be Muslims from other countries in the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: When the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade was formed, who were the members or the people that were attracted to this brigade?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, in Travnik -- they were mostly from Travnik and from the surrounding villages. These are the men who would come to the 7th Muslim Brigade. There were some men from Prijedor, Banja Luka, Kotor Varos, Mrkonjic and Jajce. So some of these men joined the 7th Muslim Brigade. Those are the men I could provide you with information about but I couldn't provide you with information about anyone else because the 7th Muslim Brigade had 63 or 72 municipalities -- or had men from 63 or 72 municipalities in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: And we speak of the ones that you could speak of, the ones that you know. Would you say that when they came or when they joined the unit, that they came trained?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: No. These men were labourers or peasants or secondary school pupils.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: My colleague asked you the question if you knew or you were familiar with a certain individual by the name of Ramo Durmis, and I believe you said yes, you knew him.

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Would you be able to assist the Trial Chamber as to how long had you known the individual Ramo Durmis, first?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: I met him around the 25th or 28th of November and then up until the 5th of January, 1993. When he left us, I didn't see him again and he didn't come to visit our unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Would you describe your relationship as very good, or how would you describe your relationship? Did you know him very well?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Well, my description of him would be very negative. I could mention an event in Travnik when he attacked a cafe. We started protecting the cafe, and from that point onwards we weren't on good terms. My unit wasn't on good terms with his unit and he wasn't on good terms with us.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: And do you know if -- do you know why he left the unit, first?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: No one ever found out why he left the unit and no one will ever find out why until he is asked for the reason.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: But certainly, during your working history you related to him as a commander, did you?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I said he left between the 5th and 10th of January, 1993, and I never saw him after that date. I haven't seen him to this very day.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Yeah, but he was there at some point in time; we agreed on that.

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I agree that he was there up until the 5th or 10th of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: And my question to you is: During that time, how did you relate to him? How did you see him, as a commander? How did you relate to him?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I have just told you the sort of relationship we had. We didn't agree on many things. We didn't agree on the way he wanted to organise his unit. So we had disagreements, misunderstandings. There were misunderstandings between my men and his men.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: But as far as you were aware and as far as you related to him in that respect, he was somebody of seniority in the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Yeah, he was. And would it surprise you if I were to say to you that there were foreigners, so to speak, Mujahedins, in the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, not necessarily in your unit but in other units? Would I be correct? Would you know that?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: I am not aware of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: You're not aware of the members of the unit that Ramo Durmis was in command?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: No, I'm not. I don't know who they were.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Was this unit very -- very, very distant from your unit?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Well, fairly so.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: My colleague showed you Exhibit D -- Defence Exhibit DK29, and it was a list of persons who had received an incentive for results achieved in the struggle on Allah's path, as it is put. And I noticed that the name Ramo Durmis is not there. I'm sure you could explain to the Trial Chamber why it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. There seems to be a mistake. It's not DK29. It should be P727.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it should be P727.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam -- Mrs. Henry-Benjamin, you said DK29; you made a mistake. It's P727.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: I apologise to you, Mr. President. I would rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: The Exhibit P727 was shown to you and it consisted a list of the following members who were awarded a monetary incentive. Do you recall seeing the list?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: And I -- I am putting it to you that the name, the individual's name, Ramo Durmis is not on the list. You'll agree with me?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Now could you tell me why it's not on the list. Do you have any idea?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we didn't decide on who would be awarded; the brigade command did. They decided which soldiers and which units should be awarded.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: But according to you, when did Ramo Durmis leave?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Ramo Durmis left between the 5th and 10th of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: So certainly he would not -- the brigade could not have awarded him anything then because he was not there then. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: This award was for combat activities in Visoko in 1992 on the 28th of February. All those who participated in the activities in Visoko were awarded.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that. Thanks. Your AOR was based in Travnik, and if I'm correct - and you can correct me if I'm wrong - is Maline in the Travnik area?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Maline was not in my zone of responsibility, but Maline is part of the municipality Travnik. But it wasn't in the zone of responsibility of the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: According to you, Maline was not in your zone of responsibility in that area?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: But could you assist us. Were you aware of what transpired in Maline on June 8th, 1993?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we couldn't have known because the communications in the area that I have marked above Travnik in the direction of Guca Gora, the road was blocked. So it was impossible for us to reach any of the units in this area here from Travnik to Maline, Mehurici, and Zenica. We were not in a position to know what was happening there.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: How did you view your role or responsibility as commander?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: My role was a very difficult one because I had to be with the men at all times, wherever they were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. It's half past 10.00 now, so we will have our break and resume at about 5 to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Henry-Benjamin, I'm giving you the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. Jusovic, I just have a couple more questions for you. First, could you state for the benefit of the Trial Chamber if at any time you ever during your tenure with the 7th Muslim Brigade if at any time you changed battalions?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: So from beginning until end, if I'm correct, you were always the commander of the 1st Company of the 1st Battalion. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: I was the commander of the 2nd Company.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Sorry --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Henry-Benjamin, on a number of occasions you've tried to make him say that he was the commander of the 1st Company, but he's always claimed that he was the commander of the 2nd Company.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: My apologies, Mr. President, but it wasn't in fact the company I was getting at but it was in fact the battalion because that has seemed to be the query around here. But I think he has clarified to us now.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: And my last question to you would be: Could you with any clarity say to the Trial Chamber or explain to the Trial Chamber the position of General Kubura in April to June 1993. Would you be able to give us any information with respect to that?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: As to Mr. Amir Kubura, I can't provide you any information. I know he was the Chief of Staff when I was with him, and as to that period you're referring to, I don't know what his duties were.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, that's the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mrs. Henry-Benjamin. For additional questions I'm now going to give the floor to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No additional questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The other Defence team.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No additional questions, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that case, I myself have a couple of questions to put to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You explained to us in replies to our questions that you were on holiday in Switzerland and that you came back and you were included in the staff of the 7th Brigade initially as a simple soldier. Could you tell the Trial Chamber what your job, your professional activity was before these events. What was your job before you became a soldier.

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: I was a machine technician and I worked at an automobile repair shop in Switzerland. So that was my job before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before those events and before getting a job in Switzerland, did you do your military service in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And where exactly did you do your military service?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: In Sombor and in Skopski Petrovac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You explained to us that at first you were a simple soldier, then head of a section, and then you were appointed commander of the 2nd Company?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you know for what reason you were appointed? Were you the most competent amongst the soldiers? What has led to you being selected and appointed as commander of the 2nd Company?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: I was an exemplary soldier. I was obedient, and I gave advice to other soldiers what and how they should do; and that's why I was appointed commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So when you were within the 7th Brigade, did you have a soldier's pay?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: There was no pay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And you had never been paid then?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: No. No money.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And as far as you know, no other member of the 7th Brigade was receiving any pay?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence earlier on showed you a document which is table number 3 with regard to the monetary, financial recompense given to members of the 7th Brigade. And your name is indicated on position number 5 in that list. Does it mean that there was never actually any money involved, that you never got this financial incentive?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now on page 17, line 19 of the transcript, when you were asked whether the 7th Brigade was ever at Maline you said of your own accord that, no, because there were no inhabitants there that could have joined the 7th Brigade. So I was a bit bothered by your reply. Are we meant to conclude then that the recruitment in as far as the 7th Brigade was concerned was geographical recruitment only? In other words, those who were members of the 1st Company came from one specific geographical area, you yourself who were in the 2nd Company with your men were from another region, et cetera. Was that the way in which it was done? In order to make it quite clear: Were soldiers recruited on the basis of only and exclusively of their geographical origin?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: No. The 7th Muslim Brigade was recruiting soldiers and soldiers were placed into battalions and then companies. We couldn't say, okay, let me have this soldier or that one. It was the command of the brigade and the battalion who were deciding about that. So that was within the area of competence of the brigade to mobilise soldiers on the basis of decision from the defence ministry. And then they were sent to battalions and companies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You've only given me a partial answer to my question. If, for example, somebody was living in Travnik, would they have been sent to one particular unit which was stationed at Travnik, for example, or else would an inhabitant of Travnik -- could they be sent to another region?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they could have been sent to another region.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. Thank you. I seem to have understood on the basis of your replies that you yourself had been appointed -- perhaps it's a mistake, but anyway. Apparently you were commander of the 1st Company in July 1993. I would just simply like to know whether you remained in the 2nd Company throughout that period of time or whether you were in the 2nd Company during the first six months of 1993 and then you were made commander of the 1st Company. Could you specify that for me, please.

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: I was a commander of the 2nd Company, and of course there were huge losses incurred. There were lots of people killed and wounded, and we were restructured, as it were. And the 3rd Company was made the 1st one. In that month, basically, we only had three companies, not four. So we had to restructure in the battalion in order to have our companies up to full strength, and that's when I was moved to the first company.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You were sent to the first company as of July 1993. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right then. And as of June 1993 -- July 1993, where were you geographically?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: We were at Travnik, Bjelovac, and Fojnica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A couple of minutes earlier you indicated that you had incurred losses and that soldiers had been killed and wounded. Your company, the 2nd Company, did it fall victim to this situation? Did you have many killed and wounded?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And in the course of what fighting?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Around Vitez, at the defence line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And that was at what time, what month?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: It was between August and October -- or rather, between July and October.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Between July and October, but what year?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My question was about the 2nd Company because according to my understanding in January, February, March, April, and June in 1993 you were the commander of the 2nd Company.

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And as of July 1993 you were made commander of the 1st Company. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Between January and July 1993 - and I'm talking about the 2nd Company only - did you have any losses, any soldiers killed or wounded?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we had killed and wounded because the operations area of that company of the 1st Battalion was quite big. So in June we had Hajdareve Njive, Huna [as interpreted], and then we had to get the Bijelo Bucje back on the 16th of June. And then we had to close that defence line. And then on the 24th of June, we had another fierce battle. There was an attack by the HVO and the Montenegrin aggressor at Vagan, Nova Rovna [phoen] and Mascema and we incurred huge losses there, so our company was decimated. More than half of our soldiers were gone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mentioned at a certain point that you had 85 men, that you had between 80 and a hundred soldiers basically. On the basis of your recollection, out of a hundred how many soldiers would you have lost?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: I never had as many as a hundred; I had about 60 soldiers. Then I got about 25 or 30 soldiers from the 1st Company, who happened to be at Travnik. And after the completion of that operation they went back to their companies of origin when we liberated a certain part of the territory. So the 1st Company was complete then. And within my company it was between 30 and 45 soldiers who had been either killed or wounded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So half of them more or less had been either killed or wounded. Now I'd like to move on to another topic. You've explained in replying to one of our questions that your company went through periods when soldiers were on leave and that at that time you would go back to Travnik to the barracks there or -- and that you would leave your weapons there and those weapons would be given to those people who were going to take your positions along the front lines. Was that the way it happened?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right then. When you relinquished your arms at the barracks, was there some kind of register, some kind of record which would indicate that on that day the 2nd Company has left 40 guns, 25 pistols, or what have you? When you left your weapons at the barracks, was there any written proof of that transaction, as it were, the exchange of arms amongst units?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Certainly, yes. Of course it was all recorded in writing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But you yourself as commander of a company, what was your -- what weapons did you have?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
utterances.text: I had an automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. When you went back to the barracks, would you keep that rifle on you or would you leave it at the barracks?

utterances.speaker: SUAD JUSOVIC
